text:
Devon Toews has spent years as the quiet half of Colorado's blue line. Nine goals in 24 games is not quiet. He has 23 points, seven on the power play, and his ice time has climbed by more than three minutes a night over his last ten games, to about 24.

Some of this is real. Over those ten games he's getting better chances on his own shots (2.2 expected goals, the quality of his looks, against 1.4 usual), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best defensemen in the league at getting to the home-plate area and setting up teammates last season. Colorado drives 60% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there.

Some of it isn't. He's shooting 20% after 3% last season, on 3.7 expected goals, and the team has scored 11.8 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey also notes he skates with very strong teammates, which flatters his raw numbers. Watch the shooting percentage drift back. The minutes and the chances are what tell you whether the role has changed.
headline: Toews finally scoring like his chances say
